title: RemindMe: Plugging a Reminder Manager into Email for Enhancing Workplace Responsiveness
research_question: Can a reminder-management layer integrated with enterprise email reduce the cognitive burden of tracking incoming and outgoing workplace requests and improve reminder handling over time?
methodology: The paper presents the design of RemindMe, drawing on prior research in social request management, interruption management, prospective memory, and cognitive psychology. The system combines an email-reminder creation algorithm with a learning mechanism intended to improve reminders over time and a user interface for reminder delivery. It is implemented as a browser plugin layered on an existing web-based enterprise email system; the accessible abstract does not describe a controlled evaluation or quantitative effectiveness study.

key_findings.finding: The system is explicitly designed around incoming and outgoing email requests rather than general email organization.
RemindMe combines automatic reminder creation with a learning mechanism intended to improve reminder behavior over time.
Reminder delivery is integrated into a user-facing email interface rather than implemented as a separate task-management application.
The browser-plugin architecture allows the reminder functionality to be added on top of an existing enterprise webmail system.
The accessible source establishes a design goal of reducing cognitive overhead but does not provide quantitative evidence that RemindMe actually improves workplace responsiveness.

limitations: Only the abstract was accessible, so details of algorithms, training data, user studies, evaluation procedures, and failure modes could not be verified.
The accessible source reports the system design and intended benefits but no quantitative evidence of reduced cognitive load or improved responsiveness.
No public code or evaluation dataset is identified in the accessible source.
The described implementation is specifically a browser plugin for web-based enterprise email, so applicability to other communication environments cannot be assessed from the abstract.
raw_claims: Sending reminders to colleagues is a common workplace activity.
The system targets the cognitive effort involved in managing email-based requests.
Both incoming requests and requests sent to other people are within RemindMe's scope.
The design draws on research about request management, interruptions, and cognitive psychology.
RemindMe contains an algorithm for creating email reminders.
The reminder mechanism includes a learning component intended to improve its behavior over time.
The system provides an interface through which reminders are delivered.
RemindMe is implemented as a browser plugin over an existing web-based enterprise email system.
